stage_a.note: Smiling, energetic, uses words like gorgeous and beautiful to describe her creations.
Animated gestures and upbeat tone when describing how she combines baked goods with flowers.
Friendly greeting, welcoming smile, very approachable demeanor throughout the pitch.

venture.description: Edible flowers baked into artisanal cookies, cakes, and other sweet treats.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria delivers her prepared pitch, introducing her edible flower baked goods and asking for investment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara laughs in response to Loria's opening question.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria invites the panel to look at and taste the samples provided to them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori tastes the cookie and comments that it is very good.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara describes the cookie as a rich buttery shortbread.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert states that the product is incredible.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark expresses amazement at the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria thanks Robert for his compliment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks Loria how she came up with the idea for the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria explains her background as a tennis player and private chef, which led to her baking for clients.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks Loria to walk them through her sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria details her lifetime sales and revenue breakdown over the past three years.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if she is selling direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms that her sales are direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the business is profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria repeats the question about profitability.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark reiterates the question, stating he wants to know if she is profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms she is very profitable, detailing the cost and retail price of a box of cookies.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori expresses surprise at the high retail price of the cookies.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much money she expects to make this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria states her profit from the previous year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria elaborates on how her business gained traction through viral photos and features in major publications.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks who handles her social media.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria states that she does everything herself.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if she works extremely long hours given her workload.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms that she works very hard.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what she is looking for in an investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria explains she wants a mentor and a partner to give her advice.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert compliments the product as a beautiful, artisanal, high-end item.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if she worries that the product's unique beauty might be lost if the business scales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria acknowledges the concern but sees opportunity to scale, mentioning a potential partnership with a major coffee chain.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if she would maintain the high price point in a mass-market setting.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria clarifies she would offer a smaller package at a lower price point.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if she intends to package it differently rather than lowering the overall price point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms she wants to offer a more accessible price point for a mass market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin notes that many competitors exist at lower price points and praises her premium model.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin states he is ready to make an offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria reacts with excitement to Kevin's statement.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that he is making an offer and frames it positively.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin offers the requested amount for a larger equity stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria asks Kevin to explain his vision for the company if they partner.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin explains he wants to keep the brand premium and help her manage the workload, justifying his equity ask.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert makes a lighthearted comment comparing Loria to a flower girl.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria asks Lori for her thoughts and if she will make an offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori praises the product but decides the business is not the right fit for her and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria thanks Lori for her time.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert praises Loria's branding efforts but states he does not see the business as investable and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria thanks Robert.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark advises Loria to focus on her premium brand rather than going mainstream, and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks for clarification on whether Loria intends to take the product out of the premium space.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria explains her desire to create a separate line of products for retail grocery stores.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if she is currently selling in retail stores.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms she is not currently in retail.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark warns that the retail space is highly competitive and difficult.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara notes that while retail is scary, Loria does not seem easily frightened.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria asks Barbara if she will make an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara considers making an offer but questions why Loria needs a partner, wanting to ensure she can add value.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria explains she needs help hiring an operations manager to handle the workload so she can focus on growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks if the investment money is intended for hiring and operations.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria confirms the funds are for operations and developing a consumer packaged goods product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara states she can help with finding the right people and signals she will make an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara offers the requested amount for a slightly higher equity stake than asked.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark encourages Loria to accept Barbara's offer immediately.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Loria accepts Barbara's offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Loria and Barbara celebrate the deal with the rest of the panel.

decisions.note: Wants to keep it premium and help build the brand.
Thinks it's a beautiful luxury item but not the right business for her.
Thinks she has done a remarkable job but doesn't see the investable side.
Believes the company is her and trying to be mainstream will backfire; not a fit.
Wants to be a valuable partner and help with operations and CPG development.
